findings.title: normalize_file leaves a leading '/' when the path starts with multiple slashes
findings.property: the normalized path is relative, i.e. never starts with '/'
findings.actual: '/a' (only one leading '/' is stripped, result is still absolute)
findings.evidence: Docstring: 'Normalizes the file path to use the POSIX path separator, and make the paths relative (remove leading "/")'. Windows-style '\\\\server' also becomes '//server' -> '/server' after one strip, and normalizing the result again changes it, so the function is not idempotent.

error.message:
assert not True
 +  where True = <built-in method startswith of str object at 0x7febdea471e0>('/')
 +    where <built-in method startswith of str object at 0x7febdea471e0> = '/a'.startswith
 +      where '/a' = normalize_file('//a')

review.title: normalize_file strips only one leading '/' or './' from paths like '//a'
review.reason: The docstring says to remove the leading "/", and the code removes exactly one leading '/' or './'. It is not a full path canonicalizer: '/./a', 'a//b' and '././a' are also left alone, and the tests never promise idempotence. '//a' is not a realistic input for the callers, which match repository-relative file paths against gitignore patterns, so the reporter is assuming a stronger contract than the function makes. A maintainer would probably see this as an edge case at most, not a defect worth a fix.
